picks.why: Corullón estate of 1999 on steep slate and quartzite terraces, from the Palacios family of Rioja and Priorat; La Faraona is the single vineyard at the head of the ladder the house built, and the library holds it as a wine record of its own.
picks.note: The library also holds the wine as w-la-faraona. Wave one's Priorat house of the family is another house and another wine; name no living member. Confirm the vineyard's rank under Bierzo's rules of 2017 (Viña Clasificada or Gran Viña Clasificada) before stating it.

picks.why: Valtuille de Abajo grower whose own labels and consultancy carried the Atlantic revival from Bierzo into Galicia; Ultreia Saint Jacques, Mencía from old vines of the valley, is the house's wide release.
picks.note: The library writes Ultreia St Jacques: confirm the label's spelling and the Bierzo DO on it. The house is named for a living man, so the prose says the house or the grower, never the name standing for the person. The family bodega is Castro Ventosa, a pick of this group: keep the two stories apart.

picks.why: Valtuille de Abajo family bodega with some of the oldest vines of the basin; Valtuille Cepas Centenarias is its Mencía from vines about a century old on the sandy valley floor.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm the label, that the vines are a century old by the house's account, and any founding year from two sources (family vineyards of the eighteenth century are told); name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Bierzo Alto bodega that began in 2000 by its own account, working old Mencía bush vines on slate and clay; Cepas Viejas is its old vine Mencía, the house's widely seen red.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house gave the name Cepas Viejas to a barrel fermented Godello in 2024 as well: the flagship is the Mencía (Dominio de Tares Cepas Viejas, Bierzo), so confirm the label and keep the two apart. Confirm 2000 from a second source.

picks.why: Cacabelos house near Pieros on the pilgrims' road, recovering old Mencía on the clay soils of the valley; Losada is its namesake Mencía, the way into a range that climbs to La Bienquerida.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The sources give 2004 and 2005 for the founding: leave founded empty unless two agree. Confirm the label (Losada, Bierzo) and La Bienquerida's Vino de Paraje (Las Chas, from 2018 by one source) from the DO.

picks.why: Rioja house of 1858 at Elciego that came to Rueda in 1972 with a Bordeaux consultant and launched cold fermented Verdejo; its Rueda Verdejo is the white with which, the region record says, modern Rueda began.
picks.note: Its home is Rioja, which wave one teaches without it; here it is the Rueda arm and a Rueda wine, and the library warns that the Rueda whites carry DO Rueda. Confirm the label for the years taught, the year 1972 and the consultant from two sources; give the consultant his dates only from two sources.

picks.why: La Seca estate founded in 1994 by a French couple, one of them of the Lurton family of Bordeaux; Belondrade y Lurton, Verdejo fermented and aged on its lees in oak, is the Rueda white the region record says showed the grape could age like white Burgundy.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm 1994 and the founders' story from two sources and name neither founder (both may be living); confirm the label carries DO Rueda.

picks.why: Toro estate of 1998 on deep sand whose old Tinta de Toro announced modern Toro; Termanthia, from ungrafted vines the phylloxera never reached, is the wine of the house that teaches why Toro's sand matters.
picks.note: The library holds Termanthia as the house's head wine and Numanthia as the middle one, and warns that the names are swapped: keep them straight and say why Termanthia is the flagship taught. Ownership is history: the founding family sold to LVMH in 2008 (the library); name no living member.

picks.why: San Román de Hornija estate of the Vega Sicilia family, its first vintage 2001; Pintia, Tinta de Toro in a polished, cellar shaped style, is the wine the region record names with Numanthia's as the start of modern Toro.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Wave one teaches Vega Sicilia in Ribera del Duero; Pintia is the same family's separate bodega in Toro, its home, with a wine of its own, so it returns here as its own house (say so). Confirm the first vintage of 2001 and the estate's founding from two sources.

picks.why: Toro family house of 1942 that bottled Toro under its own labels before the DO of 1987; Gran Colegiata, named for the town's collegiate church of the twelfth century, is its oak aged Tinta de Toro.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Founded in 1942 at Casaseca de las Chanas by most sources, the family moving into Toro later; one source makes the family's head the DO's first president in 1987: confirm from two and name no living member. Gran Colegiata is a line (Original, Crianza Roble Francés, Reserva, Campus): choose the bottling taught and name it as the label prints it.

picks.why: Navarra family of winemakers since 1647 by its own account; Colección 125, named in 1985 for 125 years of exports, is its prestige range, and the Blanco, Chardonnay of Finca Legardeta first made in 1993, is the wine the region record says showed Navarra Chardonnay could age.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house is sold as J. Chivite Family Estates: confirm the producer name for the label taught, and tell any division of the family's business as history only from two sources. Confirm 1647, the naming of 1985, the first vintage of 1993 and the label's wording (Colección 125 Blanco, lately Colección 125 Chardonnay). Its consultant of 1993 may be named with his dates (1949 to 2016) from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Olite family house whose first stone, by its own account, was laid in 1843; its late harvest Moscatel de Grano Menudo, sweet and unfortified, teaches the Navarra Moscatel the region record sets beside the rosado.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 1843 and the label (Ochoa Moscatel Vendimia Tardía, Navarra). The Rosado de Lágrima is the house's other style; its blend differs by source, so give none without the label. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Baja Montaña estate built from scattered parcels of old bush Garnacha, which the region record credits with making the world look again at Navarra's historic grape; La Dama is its Garnacha of old bush vines.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm both wines (La Dama and El Terroir), which is the house's flagship, the founding year and the vineyards' ages from two sources; the founders are a living couple, never named.

picks.why: Estate on the Ega at Aberin in Tierra Estella, recognised in 2007 as the first Vino de Pago of northern Spain; its Gran Vino is the red that carries the estate's own denomination.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The pliego de condiciones of the Pago de Arínzano (the Ministry of Agriculture) is the primary for the place and the grapes allowed; confirm 2007 and the first in the north. Older vintages are labelled Gran Vino de Arínzano and the blend differs by source (Tempranillo alone, or with Merlot): give none without the label. The Chivite family replanted it from 1988 and it changed hands in 2015: tell it as history only from two sources.

picks.why: Valdizarbe project of a Rioja Alavesa house, working old Garnacha in Navarra's cool north; Santa Cruz de Artazu is the varietal Garnacha the region record holds up as proof the north can make serious red.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. The library's Artadi (p-artadi) is the Laguardia house behind it: confirm the link, the founding year and the label from two sources, and keep Artadi's own story to a line. Name no living member of either family.

picks.why: Sant Sadurní house whose family records reach to 1551 and where Cava began in 1872; Anna de Codorníu, named for the heiress whose marriage joined the Codorníu and Raventós families, is its Chardonnay led Cava, by the region record the first Cava of the grape.
picks.note: Confirm the label taught (Anna de Codorníu Blanc de Blancs, Brut or Brut Nature) and the heiress's marriage of 1659 from two sources. The maker of 1872 may be named with his dates from two sources. Ownership is history: the family sold a majority to a fund in 2018, told with its year only from two sources.

picks.why: Sant Sadurní house of the Ferrer and Sala families, the other giant of Cava; Cordon Negro, its Brut in a black bottle, is the Cava the region record says put the wine into the world's shops.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm the founding year (1914 is told, with the Sala family's older house behind it), the families' story and the year Cordon Negro was launched from two sources; name no living member. Ownership is history: Henkell took a majority in 2018, told with its year only from two sources.

picks.why: Sant Sadurní family house of 1881, given to very long lees ageing of Xarel·lo, that left Cava for Corpinnat in 2019; III Lustros, held on its lees for years under cork, is the long aged wine the library teaches the house with.
picks.note: Confirm the label's words for the years taught (a Gran Reserva Brut Nature under Cava, Corpinnat from 2019) and its time on the lees from the house. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Sant Sadurní grower house of 1924, biodynamic, every wine Brut Nature and disgorged by hand, and a Corpinnat house; Turó d'en Mota is its single vineyard Xarel·lo from one old plot, long aged on its lees.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm 1924, the founder's dates, the vineyard's planting year (1940 is told), the lees time and whether the house was a founder of Corpinnat from two sources or the house.

picks.why: Pacs del Penedès family house of 1870; Mas La Plana, Cabernet Sauvignon of a single Penedès vineyard, put Penedès reds on lists abroad when its 1970 came first among the Cabernets at the Gault Millau Wine Olympiad in Paris in 1979.
picks.note: The 1970 was labelled Gran Coronas Black Label (Etiqueta Negra): confirm the change of name to Mas La Plana and its year, and the Olympiad of 1979, from two sources. The library warns that Grans Muralles and Milmanda are Conca de Barberà wines. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: The Dominio de Valdepusa at Malpica de Tajo, where Carlos Falcó (1937 to 2020) brought irrigation and canopy science to Cabernet and Syrah and won Spain's first Vino de Pago; Emeritus is its blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot and Syrah.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The label prints EMERITVS and the house is Pagos de Familia Marqués de Griñón. Confirm the pago's year (2002 by one source, 2003 by others: the decree decides), the blend for the years taught and the founder's dates from two sources; name no living member of the family. Valdepusa is a DO Pago of its own, not DO La Mancha: say so.

picks.why: Valdepeñas house and the plateau's volume giant, whose Viña Albali, the region record says, taught the world the words Reserva and Gran Reserva; the Gran Reserva is the Cencibel that carries the ageing law to the shelf.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Valdepeñas is a DO of its own, which the La Mancha record holds beside it: say so. The house is sold as Félix Solís Avantis: confirm the producer name, the founding year, the family's story and the label (Viña Albali Gran Reserva, Valdepeñas) from two sources.

picks.why: Villarrobledo house founded in 1947, bottling from 1961; Estola, launched in 1965, was by the house's account the first Reserva of La Mancha, the aged red the region record names for the denomination.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. 1947, 1961 and 1965 rest on the house and one competition page: confirm from a second source and hedge the first Reserva as the house's claim. The founder may be named with his dates only from two sources.

picks.why: Tomelloso co-operative founded in 1961 by one account, the voice of La Mancha's Airén; Tomillar Airén is its young dry white, the glass of the grape the plateau was built on.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 1961 from a second source and the label (Tomillar Airén, DO La Mancha). A merger with two other Tomelloso co-operatives was announced lately: tell nothing of it unless it is history with a year and two sources. The record must say it is a co-operative.

picks.why: Hunting estate in the Montes de Toledo of Ciudad Real, made a Vino de Pago of its own; its Cabernet Sauvignon is the estate red that teaches the international side of the plateau's pagos.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane: confirm from two sources the pago's year (2006 is remembered, unconfirmed), the estate's founding, that the Cabernet Sauvignon is made under that name, and whether Colección Privada is the house's flagship instead. If the pick fails, Finca Antigua of the region record is the swap, with the checker's agreement.

picks.why: Jumilla house founded in 1916 by its namesake, the first winery of the Gil family; the Etiqueta Plata, Monastrell from old vines given a year in French oak, is the wine the family's modern era began with in 2002.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Sold abroad as Silver Label and once as Juan Gil 12 Meses: confirm the label's words for the years taught and the year 2002. The founder of 1916 may be named only with his dates from two sources, else described; name no living member of the family. El Nido and Clio belong to another bodega of the family, not to this house.

picks.why: Jumilla estate farming Monastrell on its own roots; Pie Franco, from a plot of ungrafted vines planted in the 1940s, is the wine of the house the region record makes its reference for site driven, fresher Monastrell.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm the plot's planting year (1941 and 1942 are told), the family's purchase of the estate and any founding year from two sources; name no living member of the family. Las Gravas is its other red.

picks.why: Yecla family house whose Monastrell, the region record says, defines the denomination for most drinkers; Hécula, which takes an old name of Yecla, is its Monastrell from old vines.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm the founding year (1950 is told) and the founder's dates from two sources, the meaning of Hécula, and the grapes for the years taught; Solanera, a blend with other grapes, is the house's other wine.

picks.why: Jumilla family house working old ungrafted bush vines; its Dulce Monastrell, late picked and sweet, is the wine the region record makes the reference for the sweet style.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm the label, whether the wine is naturally sweet or fortified, the vineyards' place and height and any founding year from two sources.

picks.why: Yecla house of the Candela family, making wine there since 1925 by its own account; Campo Arriba, old Monastrell from the high north of Yecla, teaches the subzone the region record names for the freshest wines of the grape.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Campo Arriba is the name of the subzone and of the wine (Barahonda Campo Arriba, sold abroad as Old Vines): confirm the label and that it is the wine the house is known by; Heredad Candela, its old vine Monastrell, is the alternative. Confirm 1925 and the vines' planting (1940 is told) from two sources; the family tells of wine from about 1850.

picks.why: Lanzarote bodega whose first press, by its own account, was built in 1775, with a museum of wine in its old cellar; the Malvasía Volcánica Seco Colección is its dry white of the grape grown in pits of black ash.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house's history page is the primary for 1775; confirm the claim of the islands' oldest winery from two sources or hedge it. Confirm the vines' ages and that they are ungrafted. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Lanzarote bodega at La Florida in San Bartolomé, working Malvasía Volcánica and Listán Negro from the island's ash; Bermejo Malvasía Seco, by one account the house's star wine, is its dry white of the grape.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. 2001 is given as the founding by one source and as the remaking of an older estate by another: leave founded empty unless two agree. Confirm the label (Bermejo Malvasía Seco or Los Bermejos Malvasía Volcánica Seco). El Grifo's flagship is also a dry Malvasía: the Listán Negro rosado is the alternative if the group needs the spread, with the checker's agreement. The owner is living, never named.

picks.why: Valle de la Orotava estate in Tenerife that bottles Listán Blanco and Listán Negro from old cordón trenzado vines plot by plot; 7 Fuentes is its red led by Listán Negro, the house's widely seen wine.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm the blend (Listán Negro with Tintilla is told), the DO on the label and the founding year from two sources; name no living member of the family. Vidonia is its Listán Blanco.

picks.why: Group of four winemakers formed in the 2000s who work old own rooted vineyards in Tenerife among other places; Benje, from high old vines at Santiago del Teide in the west of the island, is the house's Canary red to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS, not in the region record and not searched in this lane. Confirm the founding year (2005 is told), the grapes, the site and the words on the label from two sources; the founders are living, never named. Táganan, from Anaga, is its other Tenerife range, and the house also makes wine in Ribeira Sacra: the record is about its Tenerife wine.

picks.why: The Fuencaliente co-operative of La Palma, the island's voice for Malvasía; its sweet Malvasía Aromática, from late picked grapes on the volcanic south of the island, is the heir the region record names to the old Canary sack.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The co-operative's name is Llanovid and Teneguía its brand: confirm both, the founding year (1945 by one source) and the label of the sweet wine taught (Teneguía Malvasía Aromática Dulce; Estelar is its long aged bottling) from two sources. The record must say it is a co-operative.

picks.why: Getaria family house on the slopes above the sea, among the growers of the Getariako Txakolina DO of 1989; its white of Hondarrabi Zuri is the classic Getaria txakoli, poured from a height.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS, not in the region record and not searched in this lane, but a Getaria house the trade knows by name. Confirm its part in the DO of 1989, the family's history (records of the seventeenth century are told) and the label from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Getaria family house with vineyards above the sea; Rubentis, its rosado of Hondarrabi Beltza with Hondarrabi Zuri, is the pink face of Getaria the region record names the house for.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane. Confirm the blend, that Rubentis is a Getariako Txakolina rosado, the family's history and any founding year from two sources; name no living member of the family. The house's white is the other wine.

picks.why: Gernika house of 1995 in the Bizkaiko Txakolina DO, with whites of Hondarrabi Zuri, some kept on their lees; Itsasmendi 7 is its fuller white, made to stand beside the Basque table.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. 1995 is told, with a move from Muskiz in 2002 by one source: confirm from two. Confirm the grapes of 7 and why it is so named.

picks.why: Bakio estate, a reference for Bizkaia's txakoli; Gorrondona, its white of Hondarrabi Zuri with a little Hondarrabi Beltza, is the house's wine to know, and its rare red of Hondarrabi Beltza is the region's other face.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the white's blend from two sources and that Gorrondona is its name on the label (Doniene is the lees aged white); by one source the red was renamed Beltza from the 2018 vintage. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Okondo estate in the Ayala valley of Álava, its first harvest in 2007, and a reference for Arabako Txakolina, the youngest of the three DOs; Astobiza is its white txakoli of the inland valley.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The sources give 2006 and 2007 for the founding (first harvest 2007): confirm from two or leave founded empty. Confirm the label (Astobiza, sold as Señorío de Astobiza) and its grapes (Hondarrabi Zuri, with Izkiriota told for some bottlings); Malkoa is its single plot white and the Izkiriota late harvest its sweet.

picks.why: O Bolo house of 2004 in the Bibei valley of Valdeorras, Godello on decomposed granite fermented and aged in large wood; As Sortes is the wine the library says established Godello as a fine white grape.
picks.note: The house is named for a living man of the Palacios family, so the prose says the house, never him; Descendientes de J. Palacios, a pick of this lane, and wave one's Priorat house are other houses of the family. Confirm the label (As Sortes, Valdeorras) and its parcels.

picks.why: Valdeorras family estate whose Guitián Godello, kept on its lees or fermented in barrel, is the wine the region record says helped make the grape's name.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane: confirm the house, its village and founding year, and the label (Guitián Godello Sobre Lías and Guitián Fermentado en Barrica are told: choose the one taught) from two sources; name no living member of the family. Godeval, of the monastery of Xagoaza, is the alternative with the checker's agreement.

picks.why: Doade house of the Amandi subzone, terracing the canyon of the Sil, and one of the founding wineries of the Ribeira Sacra DO of 1996; Pizarra, Spanish for slate, is its Mencía of the terraces.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The founding year differs by source (1980, the 1990s, 2005): leave founded empty unless two agree. Confirm that Pizarra is the flagship (the sources list it among the reds and none calls it the flagship) and its grapes; Merenzao and Brancellao are the house's native grape reds. The family are living, never named.

picks.why: Estate of the Bibei valley in Quiroga-Bibei, the region record's house for Mencía led reds and Godello from steep terraces; Lalama is its red of Mencía with native grapes beside it.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this lane: confirm the house, the label (Lalama, Ribeira Sacra), its grapes (Mencía with Brancellao, Mouratón and Garnacha Tintorera are told), the founding year and Lacima as the house's other red from two sources.

picks.why: The trading name of Ribeiro's co-operative at Ribadavia, founded by its growers in 1968; Viña Costeira, a white led by Treixadura, is the Ribeiro many guests meet first.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The co-operative's name is Vitivinícola del Ribeiro: confirm it and 1968 (its Colección 68 is named for the year) from two sources. Confirm the white's blend for the years taught; the record must say it is a co-operative.
